newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NASHVILLE EXPANSION FRANCHISE NAMES FIRST COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-NASHVILLE EXPANSION FRANCHISE NAMES FIRST COACH.

text.p: The National Hockey League expansion franchise in Nashville Wednesday named Barry Trotz as its first head coach.

Trotz, a former scout for the NHL Washington Capitals, comes to Nashville after serving as head coach and director of hockey operations for the AHL's Portland Pirates since 1993. Under Trotz, Portland captured the 1994 Calder Cup title and reached the finals in 1996.
Trotz's assistant in Portland, Paul Gardner, will join him in Nashville.
"Barry and Paul are two of the finest young coaches in all of hockey," said Nashville general manager David Poile, a former Capitals executive.
"We are fortunate to attract both of them, they've worked well as a team and deserve the opportunity to coach in the NHL," Poile said.
Nashville, which will begin play in 1998, was awarded an NHL franchise June 17. The NHL also announced plans to add teams in Atlanta, Columbus, Ohio and Minneapolis-St. Paul.
